newsitem.title: INDIA: Gold-Indian sub-continent prices seen subdued.
newsitem.headline: Gold-Indian sub-continent prices seen subdued.

text.p: Gold prices in the Indian sub-continent are expected to remain subdued in the next two weeks because of slack demand and a downtrend in international prices, dealers said on Monday.
"International prices are low. But imports are not picking up because of poor demand. Business is dull at the moment," said Bombay Bullion Association president Makhan Lal Damani.
Dealers said the sale of confiscated gold by customs had also helped improve supplies, depressing prices further.
In the week to Monday, 24 carat standard gold fell 165 rupees to 4,815 rupees per 10 grammes, after attempting a short-lived recovery.
Bullion dealers in Karachi, Pakistan's main commercial centre, said they would expect gold prices to fall this week.
"Pakistan gold prices depend on international gold markets where prices have fallen in the last few days," said dealer Farooq Qureshi.
In the week to Sunday, gold prices in Karachi fell 193 rupees to 4,702 rupees per 10 grammes.
In Dubai, the business hub of the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and the gold re-export market feeding India and Pakistan, gold demand remained subdued despite a fall in world prices.
"It is normal demand, regular buying. Nothing spectacular because the (Indian) wedding demand is over," said a trader.
India's main marriage season ran from October to February and current demand was limited, traders said.
In Bombay, Damani said he expected demand to revive at the end of the month as the summer wedding season gets underway.
Damani said the harvest of summer crops beginning in April could also raise demand for gold in rural areas.
GOLD PRICES 24 CARATS PER 10 GRAMMES IN U.S. DOLLARS
(Conversion $=35.85 Indian rupees 40.22 Pakistani rupees and 3.67 UAE Dirhams) * Bombay prices March 10/3, Karachi and Dubai March 09/02
